purpose: One service may have different official portals, documents, fees, eligibility and issuing authorities by state, district and issuing level. Store those as jurisdiction-specific records; do not infer one state checklist applies nationwide.

fields.id: stable CivicFlow internal ID, e.g. IN-BR-CASTE-CERT-CIRCLE
fields.canonical_service_id: shared canonical task ID, e.g. caste_certificate
fields.name: display name
fields.state_code: ISO-like CivicFlow state/UT code from state_ut_portals.json
fields.department: verified responsible department string and stable department ID
issuing_authority_levels: District, etc. only where source confirms
fields.official_service_url: deep-link to a specific service, not merely home page; nullable if not stable
fields.document_checklist_url: official checklist page/PDF; nullable if not found
fields.eligibility_rules: structured requirements only when backed by official notification/portal
fields.fees: amount/currency/fee type/source; use unknown if not verified
fields.department_contacts: optional official helpdesk and grievance authority

allowed_domains: exact official host and explicitly approved subdomains

language_options: languages supported by portal, if verified

important_rules: Never infer documents from a generic certificate type. Document lists vary by State, district, applicant category, age, issuing tier and scheme purpose.
Do not equate service exists on a government website with CivicFlow automation implemented.
Do not mark a service available because a portal home page responds. Verify the exact service path and current submission mode.
Keep source URLs and timestamps on every document, eligibility and fee claim.
Never send passwords, OTP, CAPTCHA, card/bank credentials or eSign secrets to the AI model.
Final submission and payment require direct citizen action/confirmation.
If the government portal blocks iframe embedding, use Member 3 remote Playwright stream in the app workspace; do not use an insecure reverse proxy to defeat portal security headers.
